newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-BECKER ARRIVES IN MIAMI, SILENT ON MOVE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER ARRIVES IN MIAMI, SILENT ON MOVE.

text.p: Tennis star Boris Becker arrived in Miami on Monday trailed by German media reports that he had left his country for good to set up home in Florida.

Becker, who is scheduled to play at the Lipton Championships in nearby Key Biscayne later this week, refused to speak to reporters waiting for him at the airport and the three-time Wimbledon champion was escorted out of the arrival area by security guards.
Becker's wife Barbara, 31, and son Noah, 3, arrived in Florida over the weekend.

The German star was reportedly planning to make his new home on exclusive Fisher Island just off Miami Beach, where fellow tennis star Jim Courier owns a home. Becker's lawyer was not immediately available to comment on whether the move was permanent.

The former world number one had said last year that he wanted to move to the United States when his son was old enough to begin school. That timetable may have been moved up by a raid by German tax investigators on Becker's Munich house in his absence in December.
After the raid, an angry Becker warned that he could leave Germany sooner.

The mass-circulation daily Bild, in a story headlined: "Boris's bitter farewell" said Becker had put his car up for sale, that Noah's room in their villa was empty and that the family had spent a farewell evening with Becker's parents.

Becker and his wife, who is black, have said they want Noah to attend school in the United States to avoid the pressures in Germany of having a famous father, and so that he might be able to lead a more normal life in a multi-racial society.
